THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR ORDERS THIS DAY, THE  COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:7611  CRL.P No. 101280 of 2024  ORDER Heard Sri Chetan Munnoli, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Praveena Y. Devareddiyavara,
learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent/State.

2. The petitioner herein is the accused No.1 in Crime No.20/2024 wherein the respondent/police have registered a case against the petitioner for the offences u/sec. 498-A, 306, 109 r/w 34 of IPC.
3.

Brief facts of the case are as under:
It is the case of the prosecution that the mother of the deceased lodged a complaint stating that she performed the marriage of the petitioner herein and her daughter 17 years ago.
The petitioner herein addicted in consuming alcohol for the past 2-3 years.
After having consumed alcohol, he was suspecting the fidelity of the deceased and used to assault and torture her one or the other pretext.
The said fact made known to the complainant by the deceased.
However, they advised her to adjust and stay in the matrimonial house.

On 15.02.2024, the deceased committed suicide in her NC:
2024:KHC-D:7611 matrimonial home by hanging herself.
After coming to know the said fact, the complainant went to the spot and lodged a complaint against the petitioner herein and others.

The jurisdictional police after registering the case,
conducted investigation and submitted the charge sheet.
4. It is the submission of learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is innocent of the alleged offence and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
There is no nexus between the death and the instigation.
The averments of the complaint did not disclose either abatement or instigation to commit suicide.
Merely because he was consuming alcohol and suspecting fidelity, cannot be ground to make out a case of abatement to commit suicide.
Moreover, the other accused in the said case have been granted bail by the Trial Court.
The petitioner being a resident of Kerur has to take care of his children.
Now, they are staying with the parents of the petitioner.
The punishment prescribed for the offence under Section 306 of IPC is maximum 10 years.
Therefore, his bail application may be considered and he may be enlarged on bail by NC: 2024:KHC-D:7611 imposing suitable conditions.
Making such submission, the learned counsel for the petitioner prays to allow the petition.

5. Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently opposed the bail petition and submitted that the petitioner herein being husband used to assault and abuse the deceased by suspecting her fidelity.

Though she has tried to adjust and stay with him, it was not possible for her Yamanappa Ashok Dhang vs The State Of Karnataka on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120577708/
2 to live with the petitioner.

sentences.text: Being frustrated the act of the petitioner, she committed suicide by leaving three children.
Therefore, it is not fit case to grant bail.
Making such submission, learned HCGP prays to dismiss the petition.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties and also perused the averments of the complaint and also FIR and charge sheet, it appears from the averments of the charge sheet that the petitioner herein was addicted in consuming alcohol and used to suspect the fidelity of the deceased.
There was a frequent quarrel between the petitioner and the deceased regarding the suspicion.
However, the averments of the charge sheet did not disclose as how the petitioner is responsible for death of NC: 2024:KHC-D:7611 the deceased.
The proximity between any quarrel or instigation and cause of death has not been forthcoming in the averments of the charge sheet.
Having considered the said fact, I am of the considered opinion that he may be enlarged on bail by imposing suitable conditions.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in Crime No.20/2024 of Ankali Police Station on executing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only) with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court, subject to the following conditions:
a) The petitioner shall appear before the trial Court regularly without fail.
 b) The petitioner shall not threaten the  prosecution witnesses nor hamper
the  proceedings of the Court

. 
 c) The petitioner shall co-operate with the investigation as and when it is required.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:7611 d) The petitioner shall mark his attendance on Saturday between 9.00 a.m. to 2.00 p.m. fortnightly basis till filing of the charge sheet.
e) The petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the Court till disposal of the case.
In case, if the petitioner violates any of the bail conditions as stated above, the prosecution will be at liberty to seek for cancellation of bail.
